entries.name: Analog

text.v: The
Analog
can do calculations on an input signal based on the comparison result of the A and B inputs.
Right Clicking on the block will bring up its GUI, with a picture of the Output (O), Input (I), and the two side inputs (A) and (B).
see overleaf for a picture and explanation of the GUI.
[TODO: Analog GUI goes here]
Below the picture of the Analog, we have three possible conditions: A = B, A is Less Than B, and A is Greater than B.

In all three conditions, we can do some basic arithmetic on the input, allowing us to multiply the strength of the input, and add to it as well. For example, you could take the input strength, double it, and add 10.

If you want to divide the signal, or take points off, you can multiply it by a number less than 1, or add a negative number respectively. For example, multiplying the strength by '0.5' is equivalent to dividing it by two, and adding  '-10' is the same as taking away 10.
Since we're working with redstone signals here, anything above 15 or below 0 is capped to full strength signal or no signal, respectively.
Isn't math fun?

entries.name: Counter

text.v: The counter is a simple block that will count redstone pulses and emit a redstone signal when it reaches a certain number. Then it starts over.
its GUI has two values - 'Counter' (the maximum number it can count up to) and 'Current' (the number it's currently at).
Once Current is equal to Counter, it emits a redstone signal. Another redstone pulse will turn off the signal and reset Counter to 0.

entries.name: Crafting Card

text.v: The Crafting Card is an item that can hold a recipe. It can be used for regular 3x3 recipes but also for more complex shapes. Various machines can use this card.
Note that stored recipes don't actually have to be valid. This card can also serve as a general way to represent 'inputs' and an 'output'

entries.name: Dialing Device

text.v: With the Dialing Device you can link a
Matter Transmitter
to a
Matter Receiver
. Note that the Matter Transmitter has to be nearby but the Matter Receiver can be very far away (even in another dimension)
Infusing
this machine reduces power usage

To dial you first have to select a Matter Transmitter. If there is only one nearby then it will be automatically selected. After that you have to select a Matter Receiver (in the bottom list) and chose either 'Dial' or 'Dial Once'. With 'Dial Once' the connection will be interrupted as soon as someone teleports

entries.name: Filter Module

text.v: The Filter Module is a very versatile item that can be used to whitelist or blacklist items for the machine. Various machines support this module (Builder, Modular Storage, Crafter, ...)
Blocks, items, and tags are supported. You can blacklist or whilelist and also require mathing on NBT and damage
Sneak right click
on an inventory (like a chest) to add all items/block in that inventory to the filter.
Sneak right click
on a block in the world to add that block to the filter.
In the GUI of the filter module you can also add tags or convert a block/item to the corresponding tags

entries.name: Logic

text.v: This block has three redstone inputs and one output. Using the GUI you can make any possible combination of those three inputs into a single output. For every input combination you can set the output to off, on or keep. In 'keep' the state of the output will be the same as it was before the input was switched to this state.

entries.name: Machine Bases

text.v: Machine Bases
are similar to
Machine Frames
in that they are a crafting material, however the resulting machines are slightly different.
Machine Bases produce machines that are a quarter of a block high, and usually have some form of
redstone
output or input.
When you place one of these machines, the direction it faces is determined by
which edge of the block your cursor is closest to
It may help to imagine an X on the side of the block you are placing the machine on, then think about which 'quarter' of the X you're looking at.
The output will be facing this direction and the input will come from the opposite direction.
This is particularly useful for placing these machines in cramped spaces or on walls - which is one of the more convenient features of these blocks.
Of course, if you don't like the direction the block is facing in, you can always
Wrench
it - just right-click with the wrench in Wrench Mode to change the direction it's facing in.
The
Machine Base
does nothing on its own, but is used in many recipes as the base for other blocks.

entries.name: Sequencer

text.v: The Sequencer is a versatile block that can generate specific sequences of redstone signal based on other redstone inputs. It works by selecting 64 different redstone outputs. Whenever a sequence runs it will set the redstone output of this block to this pattern in sequence
There are 7 different modes:

items.v: Cycle once. Ignores signals until done
Cycle once. Restart cycle on new signal
Continious loop. Signal resets cycle to start
Continious loop while enabled. Stay at current step if disabled
Continious loop while enabled. Reset to beginning if disabled
Perform one step in the cycle on every signal

entries.text:
Sequencer
The Sequencer is a versatile block that can generate specific sequences of redstone signal based on other redstone inputs. It works by selecting 64 different redstone outputs. Whenever a sequence runs it will set the redstone output of this block to this pattern in sequence
There are 7 different modes:
Once1: Cycle once. Ignores signals until done
Once2: Cycle once. Restart cycle on new signal
Loop1: Continuous loop. Ignore redstone signals
Loop2: Continious loop. Signal resets cycle to start
Loop3: Continious loop while enabled. Stay at current step if disabled
Loop4: Continious loop while enabled. Reset to beginning if disabled
Step: Perform one step in the cycle on every signal

Module Slots

entries.name: The Screen

text.v: The Screen is a versatile block that can display all kinds of information. This depends on the modules you have installed. The Screen needs power that is remotely supplied by a nearby
Screen Controller
Right click
with an empty hand to open the Screen user interface
In the GUI you can install modules (or you can install them by right clicking the module on the screen)
Many modules (like the energy module) need a target to work on. To set that target you must first
sneak right click
the module on the machine you want to monitor
When the module is installed in the Screen there are also various display options that you can set by opening the specific module GUI (accessed through the normal Screen GUI)
In that GUI you can also enable 'full bright' mode and by using the wrench you can change the size and transparency of the screen

entries.text:
The Screen
The Screen is a versatile block that can display all kinds of information. This depends on the modules you have installed. The Screen needs power that is remotely supplied by a nearby Screen Controller
Right click with an empty hand to open the Screen user interface
In the GUI you can install modules (or you can install them by right clicking the module on the screen)
Many modules (like the energy module) need a target to work on. To set that target you must first sneak right click the module on the machine you want to monitor
When the module is installed in the Screen there are also various display options that you can set by opening the specific module GUI (accessed through the normal Screen GUI)
In that GUI you can also enable 'full bright' mode and by using the wrench you can change the size and transparency of the screen

entries.name: The Screen Controller

text.v: With the Screen Controller you can power nearby
screens
. Using the 'Scan' button in the GUI you can connect to all screens in a 32x32x32 radius.
Infusing
this machine will increase this range

entries.name: The Tablet

text.v: The Tablet can be used to remotely access various machines.
Sneak right click
to open the internal tablet gui where you can install up to 6 modules. Right clicking the tablet will give you the gui of the current module. Using the
[prevDestination]
and
[nextDestination]
keys you can switch between installed modules
Note that to be able to access the remote machine it will have to be near enough or chunkloaded. If it is properly chunkloaded then the tablet will also work from another dimension

entries.name: The Tank

text.v: A container for liquids that can (by default) hold up to 32 buckets. It's possible to restrict the type of liquids by placing a bucket with the specific liquid in the filter slot

entries.name: Timer

text.v: The timer is a simple gate that will repeatedly send a redstone pulse. You can input any value for the delay so it can be used for very long timeouts

What is special about this timer is that it restart when it itself receives a redstone pulse at its input. So given timely input pulses this block will never output a pulse itself. By using this feature this block can be used as a way to detect that a certain activity is overdue

entries.name: Wire

text.v: The
Wire
simply transmits the
input signal
to the
output
. Simple, straightforward, lag free. It can only go in straight lines though.
On the upside, as with all other blocks made using
Machine Bases
, it can be placed on walls or ceilings.
